name: Zora Neale Hurston
description: Zora Neale Hurston (born January 7, 1891, Notasulga, Alabama; died January 28, 1960, Fort Pierce, Florida) was the novelist and anthropologist who carried Eatonville, Florida — the first incorporated all-Black town in the United States, where she was raised — into world literature. She studied at Howard University, where she co-founded the student newspaper The Hilltop, took her bachelor's at Barnard in 1928 under anthropologist Franz Boas, and did graduate work at Columbia. Her folklore collections Mules and Men (1935) and Tell My Horse (1938) recorded Black Southern and Caribbean life in its own voice, and her four novels — Jonah's Gourd Vine (1934), Their Eyes Were Watching God (1937), Moses, Man of the Mountain (1939), and Seraph on the Suwanee (1948) — were joined by the autobiography Dust Tracks on a Road (1942) and more than fifty stories, plays, and essays. She died in poverty and obscurity; Alice Walker placed her headstone in 1973, marking her “A Genius of the South.”

name: Zeta Phi Beta Sorority, Inc.
description: Founded January 16, 1920 at Howard University; colors Royal Blue and White; first Greek-letter organization to charter a chapter in Africa (1948); constitutionally bound to Phi Beta Sigma; chartering member of the NPHC.

name: Zinn Education Project
aliases: ZEP; Zinn Education Project: Teaching a People's History
description: The Zinn Education Project (ZEP) is a United States education project that promotes the teaching of people's history — history told through the experiences of working people, women, people of color, and organized social movements — in middle and high school classrooms. It was founded in 2008, after historian Howard Zinn referred a former student, William Holtzman, to fund an effort to bring that approach into classrooms; it is the only project Zinn allowed to bear his name. ZEP is coordinated jointly by two nonprofit organizations, Rethinking Schools and Teaching for Change, and offers hundreds of free, downloadable lessons and film and book listings organized by theme, period, and grade level, along with a daily This Day in People's History series. In CultureTechLens research, ZEP's materials library is the cited distribution source for Stanley Nelson's documentary The Black Press: Soldiers Without Swords, whose interviews include Chicago Defender publisher John Sengstacke.

name: Zainab Johnson
description: Zainab Johnson is a stand-up comedian, actress and writer whose material is shaped by her upbringing in Harlem, New York, as one of thirteen siblings in a Black Muslim family. Born in Brooklyn, she moved to Harlem at five, earned a degree in education and mathematics, and taught fifth-grade math before turning to comedy. A semi-finalist run on NBC's Last Comic Standing and a place on Variety's 10 Comics to Watch list (2019) preceded her series-regular role as Aleesha across all four seasons of Prime Video's Upload (2020–2025) and co-hosting Netflix's 100 Humans (2020); she was also a voice actor on Tab Time. Her first hour-long special, Hijabs Off, premiered on Prime Video in 2023. Her second, Toxically Optimistic — which she wrote, performed, directed and co-produced, developing it at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe — premieres on Netflix on October 27, 2026, as the first stand-up special produced by Higher Ground. CultureTechLens profiled Johnson in Short #142, published October 14, 2026.

name: Zee Nxumalo
description: Zee Nxumalo, born Zandile Nxumalo on 6 January 2003 in Eswatini and raised in Alexandra, Johannesburg, is a Swazi-South African singer and songwriter working in amapiano and Afro-pop. Her debut EP, KwaNxumalo, was released on 28 June 2022. Her breakthrough came on "Funk 55" (2023), recorded with Shakes & Les and DBN Gogo featuring Ceeka RSA and Chley, which was certified five-times platinum in South Africa and won the Motsepe Foundation Record of the Year at the 2024 South African Music Awards. She followed it with the platinum single "Thula Mabota" (2024, with Pabi Cooper and 031choppa) and the EP Inja Ye Game (2024); her single "Ngisakuthanda" reached No. 1 in South Africa and was certified three-times platinum by RiSA. Her agency biography records her as South Africa's most-streamed female artist of 2025, with "Ngisakuthanda" passing 100 million streams across platforms. In 2026 she was named to Forbes Africa's 30 Under 30 list and released Izinja Zam: Vol. 1 with Dlala Thukzin, extending a rise that has made her one of the defining young voices of amapiano.

name: Zendaya
description: Zendaya, born Zendaya Maree Stoermer Coleman on 1 September 1996 in Oakland, California, is an American actress and singer who performs under her first name alone. Trained in Oakland-area theatre programs, she first became widely known on Disney Channel, playing Rocky Blue on Shake It Up (2010–2013) and the lead on K.C. Undercover (2015–2018), which she also produced. Her adult breakthrough came as Rue Bennett, a teenager living with addiction, in HBO's Euphoria (2019–2026): she won the Primetime Emmy for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Drama Series in 2020 and again in 2022, becoming, per Britannica, the youngest winner in that category and the first Black woman to win it twice. On film she plays MJ in Marvel's Spider-Man films and Chani in Denis Villeneuve's Dune (2021) and Dune: Part Two (2024), and starred in Challengers (2024).
